The Washington Examiner presents the shift as a democratically elected partner choosing cooperation after years of Petro's obstruction — a validation of the pressure strategy. The broader argument on the right is that supply-side interdiction plus a willing host government is the fastest route to cutting cocaine flows, and that Colombian sovereignty is respected precisely because Bogotá requested the operations.

Watch for

Regional analysts expect friction over rules of engagement, evidentiary standards for strikes, and whether U.S. forces operate on Colombian soil or only offshore. Watch for congressional demands for a War Powers accounting, for coca cultivation and eradication data over the next two quarters, and for how Venezuela and Brazil respond to a permanent U.S. military footprint on the continent's Pacific and Caribbean approaches.

Sources: Washington Post Washington Examiner CEPR Colombia One

UN warns Yemen is closer to full-scale war than at any point since the 2022 truce

Facts

  • UN Special Envoy Hans Grundberg told the Security Council that Yemen faces a more serious risk of returning to large-scale conflict than at any time since the UN-mediated 2022 truce.
  • He cited the most significant intensification of military activity since that truce, including Houthi attacks in Marib, Hadramout, and Mocha, with military and civilian casualties.
  • The UN says more than half of Yemen's population is experiencing acute hardship.
  • Grundberg called for maximum restraint and protection of civilians, and warned that renewed fighting would hit a fragmented state and an economy with little capacity to absorb another shock while the wider region is at war.
  • Several Security Council members condemned the escalating Houthi attacks.

Left view

Al Jazeera and Guardian-style coverage put the humanitarian arithmetic first — a decade of war, collapsed institutions, and aid budgets already cut — and argue the Yemen front cannot be separated from the U.S.–Iran war, since escalation there raises the odds here. Coverage in this camp is skeptical that more military pressure produces anything but more displacement.

Right view

Right-of-center defense outlets and FDD's daily brief treat Houthi shipping and territorial attacks as an Iranian proxy problem that diplomacy has failed to contain, arguing the 2022 truce mainly bought Ansar Allah time to rearm. The prescription is sustained interdiction and pressure on Tehran rather than a renewed negotiating track. Mainstream U.S. coverage of Yemen is thin right now; the war with Iran is absorbing the bandwidth.

Watch for

The direct market channel is Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab shipping. With Hormuz already shut, a second chokepoint under threat would compound tanker and container rerouting around the Cape and push freight rates higher — a live inflation input. Watch insurance war-risk premiums for Red Sea transits, any Security Council product beyond statements, and whether Marib frontline movement resumes in force.

Sources: United Nations Al Jazeera The National FDD

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,786, down 0.17% Friday, slipping from Wednesday's record but capping a third straight weekly gain. Dow: 53,732, down 0.20%. Nasdaq: 26,729, down 0.28%, still barely positive for the week.
  • Oil: Both benchmarks rose Friday on Hormuz supply anxiety. Brent around $88 a barrel, up roughly 1.5% on the day; WTI near $81. The IEA is flagging that inventory buffers are running down as the strait stays shut.
  • Gas: AAA national average around $4.08 a gallon, up about 29% year over year and up from roughly $2.98 before the war began in late February. Prices had eased for a week in early August before turning up again.
  • Other: UMich preliminary sentiment 51.0 (from 55.2); one-year inflation expectations 4.3%, five-to-ten-year steady at 3.3%. Broadcom fell about 6% Friday on disappointing guidance. Futures markets still lean toward a Fed cut around September, though the energy shock cuts against it.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Scottie Scheffler shot a nine-under 61 Friday at TPC Southwind — 11 birdies, tying the course record — to lead the FedEx St. Jude Championship at 11 under, three clear of Sungjae Im and Viktor Hovland through 36 holes. Adam Scott opened with a 66. Round 3 Saturday, playoffs opener.
  • Tennis: The Cincinnati Open (ATP/WTA 1000, Lindner Family Tennis Center) runs Aug 13–23. Jannik Sinner (knee) and Carlos Alcaraz (wrist) are both out injured, leaving Djokovic — seeded third and playing his first event since Wimbledon — as a co-favorite alongside Zverev, Fritz, and Shelton. Sabalenka, defending champ Rybakina, Gauff, and Pegula headline the women's draw; Paolini and Raducanu withdrew injured.
  • Squash: PSA world rankings updated Aug 10. Men: Mostafa Asal still No. 1, with Paul Coll and Diego Elias behind him. Women: Hania El Hammamy No. 1 ahead of Amina Orfi and Nour ElSherbini. Two Americans in the women's top 10 — Olivia Weaver at 4 and Amanda Sobhy at 10.
  • WWE: SummerSlam ran two nights, Aug 1–2, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis — the first under the new domestic deal streaming exclusively on ESPN Unlimited, with Netflix carrying it internationally. Headline matches were Roman Reigns defending the World Heavyweight Title against Seth Rollins and CM Punk vs. Cody Rhodes for the WWE Championship, plus Oba Femi vs. Brock Lesnar in Hell in a Cell.
  • Hockey: Quiet mid-August, but the money keeps moving. Nico Hischier signed a five-year extension with New Jersey at an $11.7M AAV; Tyson Foerster re-upped eight years in Philadelphia; Bowen Byram signed six years at $12.5M AAV with Chicago, kicking in 2027-28. Carolina is defending its first Cup since 2006; No. 1 pick Gavin McKenna landed in Toronto.
  • Soccer: Premier League 2026-27 kicks off Friday Aug 21 — defending champions Arsenal host newly promoted Coventry City. Opening weekend also brings Hull v Manchester United, Brentford v Spurs, Newcastle v Liverpool on Sunday, and Fulham v Chelsea to close it out Monday night.
  • Football: NFL preseason Week 2 runs Aug 20–23, with Raiders at Texans on ESPN Thursday night and Seahawks at Titans on FOX Sunday. Carolina and Arizona each play a fourth exhibition this summer thanks to the Hall of Fame Game in Canton.

item.title: Fri Aug 14, 2026 — US–Iran war: Hormuz blockade to run "indefinitely" as deal stalls
item.description: US–Iran war: Hormuz blockade to run "indefinitely" as deal stalls · Trump executive order to shrink childhood vaccine schedule draws pushback · Federal judge blocks Trump's mail-in voting order nationwide · Huckabee rebukes West Bank settlers in rare US criticism
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

US–Iran war: Hormuz blockade to run "indefinitely" as deal stalls

Facts

  • The US said its naval blockade of Iranian ports can continue "indefinitely," reigniting concern over energy flows as Iran and Oman failed to finalize a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
  • Trump reiterated the US has "total control" of the strait and called the blockade a "wall of steel"; Iran's IRGC and Basij commanders insist the waterway is "under Iran's control" and will stay closed until US demands are met.
  • Hormuz transit has fallen to near three-month lows; the strait has been effectively shut since fighting began, with Iran striking shipping to snarl the route.
  • Tehran's demands to reopen include ending the blockade, sanctions relief, US troop withdrawals and war reparations.

Left view

Al Jazeera and CNN coverage frames Trump's "total control" claims as rhetoric outrunning reality on the ground, with transit data undercutting the White House and no clear diplomatic offramp — emphasizing the humanitarian and economic toll of an open-ended blockade.

Right view

Bloomberg and administration voices (Defense Secretary Hegseth) cast the blockade as effective leverage inflicting "severe economic damage" on Tehran, arguing sustained pressure forces Iran to the table rather than rewarding its demands. Right-leaning framing treats reopening on Iran's terms as capitulation.

Watch for

Energy analysts tie any Hormuz headline directly to crude: Brent and WTI ticked up Friday on the "indefinitely" comment. A prolonged closure keeps oil elevated (Brent near $88) and pressures US pump prices already at record August highs; a surprise Oman-brokered accord could trigger a sharp oil selloff.

Sources: CNN Al Jazeera Bloomberg CNBC

Trump executive order to shrink childhood vaccine schedule draws pushback

Facts

  • Trump signed an executive order Aug. 10 directing more "research and flexibility" on childhood vaccines, narrowing which shots are recommended and splitting the MMR vaccine into three separate doses.
  • Medical and public-health groups pushed back, citing decades of studies showing vaccine safety and no link to autism.
  • Legal experts say the order lacks the force of law and is likely to face court challenges; parents are unlikely to see immediate changes to vaccine access.

Left view

Washington Post and CNN coverage, plus Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand (D), call the order "reckless," warning it strips recommendations for flu and other vaccines against deadly diseases and elevates debunked claims over scientific consensus.

Right view

Rep. Nancy Mace (R) and supporters applaud the move as aligning the US schedule with international norms and "restoring parental rights," framing it as added choice and flexibility rather than a mandate against vaccination.

Watch for

Expect litigation and pushback from pediatric associations; the practical impact hinges on whether HHS/ACIP formally revise recommendations, which insurers and schools rely on. A drawn-out fight over required school shots could follow into the fall.

Sources: Washington Post CNN ABC News Rep. Mace

Federal judge blocks Trump's mail-in voting order nationwide

Facts

  • US District Judge Indira Talwani (Boston) issued a nationwide order Aug. 11 barring the Postal Service from carrying out Trump's directives to overhaul mail-in voting before the November midterms, expanding an earlier partial block.
  • Trump's March order asked USPS to build a system regulating who could vote by mail and let it refuse to deliver ballots in non-cooperating states, citing alleged noncitizen voting.
  • Talwani ruled the president "has no authority to regulate elections"; it is the second legal hold on the order, with the first pending before the Supreme Court's 6–3 conservative majority.

Left view

NPR and Votebeat frame the ruling as a check on executive overreach, stressing the judge's finding that election administration belongs to states and Congress, not the White House, and warning the order risked disenfranchising voters.

Right view

Fox News coverage centers the administration's stated goal of election integrity and preventing noncitizen voting, and notes the fight is not over — a favorable Supreme Court ruling could revive the order's core provisions.

Watch for

All eyes on the Supreme Court, which could rule before ballots are printed. The outcome shapes mail-voting mechanics in swing states for a midterm that will decide control of Congress.

Sources: NPR Axios Bloomberg Fox News

Huckabee rebukes West Bank settlers in rare US criticism

Facts

  • US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee condemned some Israeli settlers in the West Bank, referring to a group as "terrorists" — an unusual rebuke from a strongly pro-Israel envoy.
  • His comments followed a multi-night standoff between dozens of settlers and Palestinian families occupying three homes in the West Bank.
  • Settler violence in the West Bank has escalated amid the broader regional conflict.

Left view

Outlets covering the story note the significance of even a Trump-aligned ambassador breaking to call out settler violence, framing it as belated acknowledgment of a long-documented pattern that Palestinian advocates say has gone unpunished.

Right view

Right-leaning framing emphasizes Huckabee's continued strong support for Israel and reads the remark as isolating a fringe minority rather than indicting Israeli policy — a distinction between lawbreakers and the settlement enterprise itself. Mainstream US coverage of this specific incident is thinner than wire reporting from abroad.

Watch for

Whether the rebuke prompts Israeli enforcement action against settlers, and how it lands with Netanyahu's coalition. Analysts watch for friction between Washington and Israel's right flank while the US-Iran war dominates the region.

Sources: WORLD Euronews

Senate punts crypto "Clarity Act" to September

Facts

  • The Senate left for its five-week August recess without voting on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, the sweeping crypto market-structure bill.
  • Majority Leader John Thune filed to tee up a procedural vote for when the Senate returns in mid-September.
  • Sticking points remain on government-ethics rules, law-enforcement provisions, and stablecoin yield/rewards.

Left view

Democratic critics (per CoinDesk/CNBC) argue the bill lacks sufficient anti-money-laundering safeguards and strong ethics provisions, pushing to let state attorneys general enforce a ban on officials running crypto businesses — a jab at conflicts around the administration's own crypto ventures.

Right view

Republican backers frame the delay as procedural, not fatal, and cast clear market rules as overdue certainty for a US crypto industry they say has been driven offshore by regulation-by-enforcement. WSJ/industry voices see September passage as achievable.

Watch for

Limited September working days before midterm campaigning could squeeze the window. Bitcoin ETF inflows have stayed strong despite the delay; a stalled bill keeps regulatory uncertainty hanging over exchanges and token issuers.

Sources: CNBC CoinDesk Davis Wright Tremaine

Progressives keep winning primaries as midterm map firms up

Facts

  • Minnesota Gov. Peggy Flanagan won the Democratic Senate primary, extending a run of progressive wins over centrists.
  • In the GOP governor's primary, Trump-endorsed Mike Lindell lost to state House Speaker Lisa Demuth, who will face Democratic Sen. Amy Klobuchar in the fall.
  • Earlier in the month, the Senate confirmed Todd Blanche as attorney general 50–49; a South Carolina special-primary runoff between Sen. Darline Graham and Rep. Ralph Norman looms later this month.

Left view

NPR-style coverage frames Flanagan's win as evidence of energized progressive base ahead of the midterms, arguing the party's left flank is setting the agenda on economic and health messaging.

Right view

Conservative outlets read Lindell's loss as the GOP base favoring electability over loyalty tests, and cast progressive primary wins as gifts to Republicans in swing seats — betting Demuth vs. Klobuchar is more competitive than polls suggest.

Watch for

These primaries shape the battle for a closely divided Congress. Control of the Senate and House will determine the fate of stalled items like the crypto bill and the reach of Trump's executive orders now tangled in court.

Sources: NPR CNN Politics CNBC

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: Closed at a record 7,798.99 Thu (+0.65%), above 7,800 intraday for the first time; futures roughly flat Fri. Dow: 53,839.99 (+0.13%). Nasdaq: 26,803.03 (+0.81%), led by Meta, Micron, Netflix.
  • Drivers: Cooler-than-expected July inflation eased Fed rate-hike fears and fueled the record run; markets heading for a winning week.
  • Oil: Brent ~$87.9/bbl and WTI ~$82.1 rose Fri after the US said the Iran blockade could run "indefinitely"; Hormuz risk keeps a premium in crude.
  • Gas: National average ~$4.03/gal (Aug 12) — a record high for this late in the calendar year, up in every state from a year ago.
  • Crypto: Bitcoin ETF inflows stayed strong even as the Senate delayed the Clarity Act to September.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: FedEx Cup Playoffs open with the FedEx St. Jude Championship (Aug 13–16, TPC Southwind, Memphis), 70 players, no cut — first of three legs before the East Lake finale.
  • Tennis: Cincinnati Open (ATP/WTA 1000) rolls on; defending champ Iga Swiatek back, but Sinner (knee) and Alcaraz (wrist) both sitting out injured.
  • Squash: PSA action at the Valencia Memorial (Aug 11–15) and Karachi; Mostafa Asal leads the men's world rankings, Hania El Hammamy the women's.
  • WWE: Post-SummerSlam fallout continues — Roman Reigns retained the World Heavyweight title over Seth Rollins; Big Cass returned after eight years away.
  • Hockey: NHL offseason churns on after Carolina's first Cup since 2006; Ovechkin re-upped with Washington (1 yr), while RFAs Jason Robertson and Adam Fantilli and UFA Patrick Kane remain unsigned.
  • Soccer: Premier League 2026/27 kicks off Aug 21 — champions Arsenal host promoted Coventry in the Friday opener; late start allows recovery from the World Cup.
  • Football: NFL preseason Week 1 in full swing (Aug 13–15, all 32 teams); regular season opens Sept 9 with a Patriots–Seahawks Super Bowl rematch.

item.title: Thu Aug 13, 2026 — Strait of Hormuz standoff drags on as Trump insists U.S. is in "total control"
item.description: Strait of Hormuz standoff drags on as Trump insists U.S. is in "total control" · Gas hits highest-ever level for mid-August as pump pain becomes political · Karoline Leavitt to step down as White House press secretary at month's end · July inflation cools slightly, keeping the Fed on hold into September
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Strait of Hormuz standoff drags on as Trump insists U.S. is in "total control"

Facts

  • Trump reiterated on Truth Social that the U.S. has "total control" of the Strait of Hormuz and warned Iran would "get blown away" if it acted; Iran's foreign ministry publicly declared the strait blocked, and FM Abbas Araghchi denied Tehran is in direct talks with Washington.
  • Iran-Oman negotiations over inbound/outbound shipping lanes have run three-plus weeks with broad agreement on routes but no final deal; tankers have been largely unable to transit since Iran closed the waterway when fighting resumed in July.
  • U.S. Central Command said it disabled a Panama-flagged cargo vessel that tried to break the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports; Houthi forces killed six aboard a cargo ship in the Bab el-Mandeb strait — the first Red Sea shipping fatalities in over a year — and claimed an earlier strike on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery.
  • The strait carried roughly one-fifth of global oil supply before the war; the IEA-tracked forecast now sees global supply falling about 4.3 million barrels/day.

Left view

Left-leaning and mainstream outlets stress the gap between Trump's rhetoric and facts on the ground: NPR frames the war and resulting price spike as having driven his economy approval to around 31%, and notes voters who backed him to lower costs and avoid foreign wars are getting the opposite. A Washington Post opinion piece argued Trump is wrong to scapegoat oil companies for prices the war itself is driving. Sen. Chuck Schumer questioned how durable any reopening deal would even be.

Right view

Fox News amplified administration voices: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Iran now faces "someone that actually takes action," and VP JD Vance described talks as being in "the middle of the game" with the goal of maximizing oil flow. Notably, some hawks broke with the White House — former Defense Secretary Mark Esper (via Fox) warned that letting Iran and Oman help administer strait traffic could be a "very bad outcome" for the U.S.

Watch for

Analysts tie near-term oil to the deal odds: Brent hovered near $89-90 and WTI in the low $80s, with any breakdown in Oman talks or fresh Houthi strikes seen pushing crude back toward triple digits. A reopening would ease pump prices before the midterms; continued closure keeps gasoline elevated and pressures Republicans on affordability.

Sources: CNN CNBC Al Jazeera Fox News NPR

Gas hits highest-ever level for mid-August as pump pain becomes political

Facts

  • AAA put the national average for regular at about $4.03/gal as of Aug. 12, roughly $0.16 higher than a month earlier and up sharply from around $2.98 before the Iran war.
  • GasBuddy said the average is at its highest-ever level this late in the calendar year — no prior year saw the average above $4 after Aug. 12.
  • State spread is wide: California ($5.66), Hawaii ($5.45) and Washington ($5.13) highest; Texas ($3.60), Indiana ($3.61) and Mississippi ($3.65) lowest.
  • Trump has directed the DOJ to investigate Big Oil for possible price gouging, publicly pressured Exxon and Chevron over profits, and is weighing extending a Jones Act waiver.

Left view

The Washington Post editorial/opinion side calls it misdirection to blame refiners when the war-driven crude spike is the cause, arguing the administration owns the geopolitical decisions behind higher prices. Coverage in outlets like NPR and Yahoo highlights voters who feel Trump broke a core promise to bring costs down.

Right view

Fox News frames the squeeze as a byproduct of ending years of "radical climate" energy policy and points to price gouging by oil majors, echoing the White House. The Washington Examiner reported Trump warning prices "may have to" rise further as leverage against Iran, casting the pain as a temporary cost of a hard line.

Watch for

Energy analysts say a Jones Act waiver alone is unlikely to move pump prices much (OilPrice.com); the real lever is Hormuz reopening. With midterms ahead, sustained $4+ gas is the affordability metric strategists in both parties are watching most closely.

Sources: AAA The Hill Yahoo Finance Fox News Washington Post

Karoline Leavitt to step down as White House press secretary at month's end

Facts

  • Trump announced in a Truth Social post that Leavitt will leave at the end of August to spend more time with her two young children, saying he "totally" understands and respects the decision.
  • Leavitt called it a "bittersweet decision," citing the constant demands of the role; no successor has been named.
  • Her farewell post on X briefly carried a "Made with AI" label that was later removed with no explanation from X or the White House.

Left view

Left-leaning commentary (Mediaite, Axios coverage) focused on the lack of a ready replacement as a sign of West Wing disorder, and some tied the timing to broader turbulence, noting the odd "Made with AI" flag on her goodbye message.

Right view

Right-leaning coverage largely took the family explanation at face value and praised her tenure as a combative, effective communicator, framing the departure as a personal choice rather than a sign of trouble.

Watch for

Former GOP comms director Mike Dubke (via CNN) said he was "very surprised" there is no obvious deputy waiting in the wings — the succession pick will signal whether the White House wants continuity or a reset in messaging heading into the fall campaign.

Sources: Axios The Hill PBS NewsHour Mediaite

July inflation cools slightly, keeping the Fed on hold into September

Facts

  • The July CPI (released Aug. 12) rose 0.1% on the month and 3.4% year over year; core CPI rose 0.2% monthly and 2.5% annually — each down 0.1 point from June.
  • The reading came in roughly in line with expectations, easing pressure for a rate hike after a weak July jobs report.
  • Stocks were steady-to-higher on the data; the VIX fell nearly 5% and equity futures edged up Thursday as oil eased.

Left view

Progressive-leaning economists emphasize that inflation stuck above target largely reflects war-driven energy costs and tariffs, arguing everyday affordability — not Wall Street calm — is what households feel.

Right view

Market-and business-oriented conservative coverage (CNBC, WSJ readership) frames "in-line" inflation as vindication that the Fed can avoid hikes, and credits resilient earnings and AI-driven growth for keeping markets afloat despite the energy shock.

Watch for

Most analysts now expect the Fed to hold at the September FOMC meeting rather than cut, with labor-market softness and energy volatility cited as offsetting risks. Gas and Hormuz remain the wildcard that could reignite headline inflation.

Sources: CNBC BLS Yahoo Finance

Midterm maneuvering: mail-in voting order blocked, crypto bill advances, primaries reshuffle

Facts

  • A federal judge expanded a block on part of Trump's order restricting mail-in voting for the fall midterms, barring the Postal Service from carrying out the directives nationwide.
  • Before recess, the Senate advanced a landmark crypto bill and passed a short-term funding bill to avert a shutdown; a Russia sanctions bill associated with Sen. Lindsey Graham cleared the Senate for the House.
  • Primary results favored progressives in spots: Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan won the Democratic Senate primary; in Wisconsin, David Crowley took the Democratic nod for governor and will face GOP Rep. Tom Tiffany.

Left view

The Guardian/NPR-style framing treats the mail-in ruling as a check on an effort they characterize as voter suppression, and casts progressive primary wins as momentum for the party's left flank over centrists.

Right view

Right-leaning outlets (NY Post, Washington Examiner) emphasize election-integrity arguments behind the mail-in order and frame the judge's block as judicial overreach, while touting the crypto and Russia-sanctions bills as GOP-driven wins.

Watch for

With affordability and the Iran war weighing on Trump's numbers, strategists see the mail-in litigation and candidate quality shaping a tight fight for House and Senate control. Expect appeals on the voting order and House action on the crypto and sanctions bills after recess.

Sources: NPR CNBC Fox News

DOJ charges former Southern Poverty Law Center official with fraud

Facts

  • The Justice Department charged a former SPLC official with fraud, alleging she shared a bank account with a paid neo-Nazi informant.
  • Prosecutors say the center paid more than $4 million to people embedded inside extremist groups.
  • The SPLC has not been charged; the case centers on the individual official's alleged conduct.

Left view

Left-leaning observers urge caution pending evidence, noting paid informants inside extremist movements are a longstanding (if fraught) monitoring tactic, and warn against using one official's alleged misconduct to discredit civil-rights watchdog work broadly.

Right view

Conservative outlets (NY Post, Washington Examiner) treat the charges as validating years of criticism that the SPLC's "hate" designations and finances deserve scrutiny, casting it as accountability for an organization they view as partisan.

Watch for

Watch whether the indictment stays narrow to the individual or widens; the case is likely to fuel renewed political fights over the SPLC's nonprofit status and its influence on how "extremism" is defined.

Sources: WORLD CNBC

Markets & Economy

  • Stocks: Wall Street closed mixed Wednesday after the in-line July CPI — S&P 500 and Nasdaq edged higher on cooling inflation and strong earnings, Dow slightly lower. Futures ticked up Thursday (Dow +0.2%, S&P +0.2%, Nasdaq +0.1%) as the VIX fell ~5%.
  • Oil: Brent near $89 (dipping ~2% in Thursday pre-market toward $87), WTI in the low $80s (~$81-83), whipsawing on Hormuz deal odds and Houthi attacks.
  • Gas: National average ~$4.03/gal (AAA) — highest ever for mid-August; up from ~$2.98 pre-war. CA highest (~$5.66), TX lowest (~$3.60).
  • Rates/inflation: Headline CPI 3.4% y/y, core 2.5%; markets now expect the Fed to hold in September rather than cut.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: FedEx Cup Playoffs open today — the FedEx St. Jude Championship (Aug. 13-16) at TPC Southwind, Memphis, with the top 70 and no cut. Field narrows to 50 at next week's BMW Championship before the $40M Tour Championship at East Lake.
  • Tennis: Cincinnati Open main draw begins today (ATP/WTA 1000, Mason, OH) — but Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz are out injured. Djokovic and Zverev headline the men; Sabalenka and Rybakina the women. Serena and Venus Williams reunite in doubles on a wild card. Final tune-up before the US Open.
  • Squash: PSA Tour offseason lull — the 2025-26 tour has wrapped its major World Events, with fresh news posts this week previewing the 2026-27 calendar. No marquee tournament in play mid-August.
  • WWE: Fallout from SummerSlam (Aug. 1-2, U.S. Bank Stadium, Minneapolis) continues to drive programming, headlined by the Seth Rollins-Roman Reigns world-title feud and a new interim women's title picture as the road to fall premium live events takes shape.
  • Hockey: NHL dead season, but storylines simmer — Dylan Larkin reportedly requested a trade (eyeing Minnesota, Vegas or Florida), Connor Hellebuyck's future in Winnipeg is in question, and San Jose's Macklin Celebrini signed a 5-year, $18.8M-AAV extension, the richest per-season deal in league history.
  • Soccer: Premier League 2026-27 kicks off Friday, Aug. 21 — defending champion Arsenal opens at home against newly promoted Coventry City. Fixtures and TV slates are set for all 380 matches.
  • Football: NFL preseason is underway (all camps opened by July 28); roster cutdown to 53 is Aug. 30. The season kicks off Sept. 9 with a Super Bowl LX rematch, Patriots at defending-champion Seahawks, on NBC.

item.title: Wed Aug 12, 2026 — July inflation report lands as markets watch for a Fed rate cut
item.description: July inflation report lands as markets watch for a Fed rate cut · Trump signs order to shrink the childhood vaccine schedule · US–Iran tensions flare again, pushing oil higher · Colombia digs out from its strongest earthquake in years
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

July inflation report lands as markets watch for a Fed rate cut

Facts

  • The Bureau of Labor Statistics released the July Consumer Price Index at 8:30 a.m. ET today.
  • Economists surveyed by Dow Jones expected headline inflation of 3.4% year-over-year, down from 3.5% in June.
  • Core CPI (excluding food and energy) was projected to rise 0.2% on the month and ease to 2.5% annually.
  • Average hourly wage growth of about 3.2% is still running below headline inflation.

Left view

Outlets like NPR and the Washington Post frame stubborn 3%-plus inflation and wages lagging prices as evidence that tariffs and trade disruptions are quietly taxing households, arguing the Fed should be cautious about declaring victory.

Right view

The WSJ editorial page and CNBC-cited analysts emphasize the cooling trend and easing energy costs as a sign disinflation is on track, pressing the Fed to move toward rate cuts to support growth rather than keeping policy tight.

Watch for

Economists note the print heavily shapes odds of a September Fed cut; a soft reading could lift equities and pull Treasury yields lower, while an upside surprise driven by energy would revive tariff-and-oil inflation worries.

Sources: BLS NBC News Kiplinger CNBC

Trump signs order to shrink the childhood vaccine schedule

Facts

  • President Trump signed an executive order Monday calling to reduce the number of recommended childhood shots to 11.
  • The order recommends splitting the combined MMR (measles, mumps, rubella) vaccine into three separate shots.
  • It directs federal agencies to study the schedule and report back within 90 days; it makes no immediate changes to vaccine access.
  • Trump referenced autism repeatedly at the signing, though the order text does not address it; the vaccine-autism link has been repeatedly debunked.

Left view

ABC News, the Washington Post and NPR highlight sharp pushback from pediatricians and public-health groups, stressing decades of studies backing the current schedule and warning that splitting MMR into separate shots is untested and could lower coverage.

Right view

The White House frames it as "gold standard" recommendations restoring parental choice and scientific scrutiny; supportive commentators cast it as accountability for a public-health establishment they say lost public trust during the pandemic.

Watch for

The real fight comes when agency reports land in ~90 days; medical societies may keep issuing their own guidance, and insurers, states and school-mandate rules could diverge from any revised federal schedule.

Sources: ABC News Washington Post NPR White House CNBC

US–Iran tensions flare again, pushing oil higher

Facts

  • Oil prices rose after a renewed escalation between the US and Iran, with Brent crude climbing toward roughly $91 a barrel from about $83 earlier in the week.
  • The flare-up threatens a fragile ceasefire from the US–Israel conflict with Iran that began earlier in 2026.
  • Markets are again focused on shipping risk through the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint for global energy flows.
  • Separately, Russia released an American military veteran held for four years, allowing his return to the US.

Left view

Guardian and Al Jazeera coverage stresses the human and diplomatic costs of repeated escalation, questioning whether aggressive US rhetoric and strikes make a durable Hormuz deal harder and raise the risk of a wider regional war.

Right view

Fox News and allied commentators frame Trump's hard line — including his blunt threat to "beat" Iran — as necessary deterrence to keep the strait open and force Tehran back to terms, arguing weakness invites more provocation.

Watch for

Energy analysts warn any actual disruption to Hormuz traffic could spike crude sharply and feed back into gasoline and inflation; a de-escalation or prisoner-swap goodwill could just as quickly unwind the oil premium.

Sources: The Hill Al Jazeera Trading Economics NPR

Colombia digs out from its strongest earthquake in years

Facts

  • A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck western Colombia on Aug. 10, with the epicenter near San José del Palmar, about 150 miles west of Bogotá.
  • The confirmed death toll has climbed past 200 (reports around 224), with thousands injured and many still missing.
  • Colombia's Geological Service has logged more than 70 aftershocks; the government declared a national disaster and deployed the military.
  • Collapsed structures included pediatric and neonatal wards of a hospital in Cali; rescuers pulled survivors from rubble more than a day later.

Left view

NPR and Al Jazeera coverage emphasizes underinvestment in an impoverished region, building-code gaps and the need for robust international humanitarian aid to reach isolated communities near the epicenter.

Right view

With little explicitly partisan framing, right-leaning coverage is thin; outlets like Time and NBC focus on the government's disaster response, logistics of the rescue effort and the scale of the rebuild ahead.

Watch for

Aid agencies warn the toll will likely keep rising as crews reach the epicenter; watch for disease and shelter risks among the displaced and pressure on President Petro's government over relief speed.

Sources: CNN Al Jazeera NPR Time

Senate crypto "market structure" bill inches toward a floor vote

Facts

  • On Aug. 8, the Senate acted to advance the CLARITY Act crypto market-structure bill before leaving for August recess.
  • Majority Leader John Thune set up a key procedural vote for when the Senate returns in mid-September, teeing up a possible full floor vote.
  • The bill merges Senate Banking and Agriculture Committee frameworks and includes a ban on presidents and federal officials issuing or sponsoring crypto.
  • Passage needs all voting Republicans plus at least eight Democrats; ethics provisions remain the sticking point.

Left view

Democrats including Sens. Alsobrooks and Gallego, per CNBC and Roll Call, insist on tougher conduct rules — pointing at the president's own crypto ventures — and warn light-touch regulation risks another investor blowup.

Right view

Republicans and industry-aligned outlets frame the bill as overdue regulatory "clarity" that keeps crypto innovation and jobs in the US, arguing endless delay drives the sector offshore.

Watch for

The September procedural vote is the real test; a deal on ethics language could unlock bipartisan passage and boost digital-asset markets, while a stall keeps the sector in regulatory limbo.

Sources: CNBC Roll Call Forbes CNBC

DR Congo Ebola outbreak becomes the country's largest on record

Facts

  • Congolese officials report more than 2,000 deaths out of roughly 4,381 confirmed cases — the DRC's largest Ebola outbreak ever and one of the fastest-growing.
  • It is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment.
  • The WHO says the outbreak is intensifying at an "exceptional" pace and has urged a major scale-up of response.
  • The US State Department announced an additional $242 million for Ebola response in the DRC and Uganda.

Left view

Guardian and UN-cited coverage stresses global-health solidarity and warns that cuts or gaps in international funding leave outbreaks to spread, urging robust aid and support for overstretched local health workers.

Right view

Right-leaning coverage is thin here; where present, the emphasis is on accountability for how aid dollars are spent and on border and travel screening to keep the outbreak contained rather than open-ended commitments.

Watch for

Health officials warn the toll could keep climbing without a vaccine for this strain; watch for cross-border spread into Uganda and strain on the response as new treatment centers open.

Sources: Euronews UN News US State Dept MSF

Markets & Economy

  • Stocks: US futures were modestly higher early Wednesday ahead of the CPI print — S&P 500 futures ~+0.1%, Nasdaq-100 ~+0.25%, Dow roughly flat. Tuesday closed lower: Dow and S&P 500 each about −0.3%, Nasdaq about −0.6%.
  • Oil: Brent climbed toward ~$91/bbl on renewed US–Iran tensions and Strait of Hormuz risk, up from ~$83 earlier in the week.
  • Gas: AAA national average around $4.06/gal (as of Aug. 6) — down from ~$4.10 a week earlier but up sharply from ~$3.14 a year ago. Cheapest: Indiana (~$3.55); priciest: California (~$5.62).
  • Other: Markets pricing a ~56% chance the S&P opens higher (Polymarket); today's inflation reading is the key swing factor for September Fed-cut odds.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: FedEx Cup Playoffs open Thursday with the FedEx St. Jude Championship (Aug. 13–16, TPC Southwind, Memphis) — top 70 players, no cut. BMW Championship and Tour Championship follow.
  • Tennis: Cincinnati Open (ATP/WTA 1000) is underway (Aug. 13–23) as a US Open tune-up. Sinner and Alcaraz are out injured; Sabalenka, Rybakina, Gauff and Pegula lead the women, with Djokovic, Fritz and Shelton among the men.
  • Squash: PSA action continues on the calendar with a World event in Valencia, Spain (Aug. 11–15) and Budapest, Hungary later this month (Aug. 24–28) as the 2025–26 season winds down.
  • WWE: Fallout from SummerSlam (Aug. 1–2, Minneapolis) rolls on — Roman Reigns retained the World Heavyweight title over Seth Rollins, Liv Morgan kept the Women's title, and Kevin Owens returned to win a No. 1 contender's match.
  • Hockey: Dog days of the NHL offseason — Macklin Celebrini signed a five-year, $18.8M-AAV extension (highest per-season pay in league history); Patrick Kane re-signed with Chicago; Dylan Larkin's trade request lingers in Detroit.
  • Soccer: Premier League 2026–27 kicks off Aug. 21 (Arsenal vs. Coventry City), a week late due to the summer World Cup. The Community Shield (Arsenal vs. Man City) is set for Aug. 16 in Cardiff.
  • Football: NFL preseason's first full week begins Aug. 13; 53-man roster cutdown is Aug. 30. Watch position battles like Vikings QB (Murray vs. McCarthy) and Packers RB Josh Jacobs' injury/legal situation.

item.title: Tue Aug 11, 2026 — Hormuz standoff drags on as oil spikes and a US–Iran deal slips further away
item.description: Hormuz standoff drags on as oil spikes and a US–Iran deal slips further away · Trump extends China tariff pause another 90 days, hours before truce expired · Weak July jobs report reshapes the Fed's September calculus · Ukraine leans on long-range drones as Zelensky presses for US air defense
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Hormuz standoff drags on as oil spikes and a US–Iran deal slips further away

Facts

  • Oil jumped roughly 5% Monday as doubts grew that Washington and Tehran will strike a deal to restore commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, per CNBC and Reuters.
  • Shipping through the strait — normally about a fifth of global oil supply — has effectively collapsed since the conflict reignited; MarineTraffic counted 8–15 transits a day early this month versus roughly 130 before the war.
  • Iran's Supreme National Security Council says reopening requires the US to lift its naval blockade and sanctions, withdraw regional forces, pay reparations, and release frozen assets — terms Washington rejects.
  • Iran and Oman have reportedly agreed on coordinates for a proposed safe shipping corridor, but no deal is finalized.

Left view

NPR and CNN frame this as a self-inflicted crisis: a CNN analysis likens Trump's predicament to Jimmy Carter's, with a stalled economy and rising prices heading into the midterms. Sen. Adam Schiff (D-CA) argues the US went from a bad deal to renewed strikes, another blockade, and turmoil that only pushes prices higher, and Democrats are pressing to reassert congressional war powers.

Right view

Fox News highlights Trump's ultimatum framing — reopen the strait or face military action — and Rep. Mike Turner (R-OH) argues the strait can be reopened without a ground war. But the coalition isn't uniform: Republicans Rand Paul, Susan Collins and Lisa Murkowski joined efforts to limit the president's war powers.

Watch for

Analysts tie every headline here directly to crude: sustained disruption keeps Brent elevated and feeds pump prices into the fall. A credible corridor deal could unwind much of the risk premium quickly; a collapse in talks or a fresh tanker incident could spike oil further and complicate the Fed's rate path.

Sources: CNBC Al Jazeera CNN NPR Fox News

Trump extends China tariff pause another 90 days, hours before truce expired

Facts

  • Trump signed an order Tuesday extending the pause on a scheduled hike of reciprocal tariffs on China to 125%, keeping the current truce in place for roughly another 90 days, per PBS NewsHour, NBC News and CBS News.
  • The extension preserves the arrangement in place since May, under which the US charges about 30% and China about 10% while negotiators keep working.
  • It's the second such extension of the year; the prior truce was set to lapse this week.

Left view

PBS NewsHour and other mainstream outlets stress the whiplash of governing by deadline: repeated 90-day pauses leave importers and manufacturers unable to plan, and the underlying tariffs still raise costs that the Tax Foundation estimates fall largely on US buyers.

Right view

Trump and supportive outlets cast the extension as leverage working — buying time for a broader deal with Xi while keeping the threat of 125% duties on the table. Trump said he takes Beijing "at their word" on commitments made so far.

Watch for

Markets welcomed the reprieve — equity futures firmed — but economists warn the reprieve is temporary and the next cliff lands in the fall. Watch whether talks produce anything durable on rare earths, agriculture and tech export controls before the clock runs out again.

Sources: PBS NewsHour NBC News CBS News Tax Foundation

Weak July jobs report reshapes the Fed's September calculus

Facts

  • US employers cut 23,000 jobs in July versus a forecast gain of roughly 80,000 — a sharp miss, per CNBC and Fox Business.
  • Prior months were revised down hard: May cut to 63,000 from 129,000; June to 20,000 from 57,000.
  • Wage growth slowed to 3.2% year over year, the weakest since 2021; labor-force participation fell to 61.4%, a multi-year low.
  • Odds of a September rate hike fell from about 57% to 44%; next week's inflation data is seen as decisive.

Left view

Yahoo Finance and NPR-adjacent coverage read the data as evidence the labor market is cracking under the weight of tariffs and the Iran-driven energy shock, arguing the Fed should hold or ease rather than risk tipping the economy into recession before the midterms.

Right view

Fox Business and market commentators note the twist: soft jobs plus tariff-driven price pressure raises the specter of stagflation, and some argue the Fed shouldn't cut prematurely with inflation risks from oil still live. The data cut hike odds but didn't take a hike fully off the table.

Watch for

Barclays and Goldman now flag a possible cut path; all eyes are on next week's CPI. A hot inflation print alongside weak jobs would sharpen the stagflation debate and could whipsaw both bonds and equities.

Sources: CNBC Fox Business Yahoo Finance AOL / Reuters

Ukraine leans on long-range drones as Zelensky presses for US air defense

Facts

  • Ukraine has hit Russian oil facilities with long-range drones on a near-daily basis in recent months, contributing to fuel shortages inside Russia, per NPR and Reuters.
  • Russia said it downed 605 Ukrainian drones over its territory and Crimea around Aug. 6; Russian strikes on eastern Ukraine killed at least six overnight that day, per Al Jazeera.
  • Zelensky has appealed for additional US air-defense missiles; US-mediated talks have not produced a ceasefire, with the sides split over territory and security guarantees.

Left view

The Guardian and NPR emphasize Ukraine's civilian toll from Russian barrages and frame continued Western air-defense support as essential; a Ukrainian negotiator argues sustained drone strikes on Russian energy could force Moscow toward a ceasefire.

Right view

Right-leaning outlets are more divided: some back arming Ukraine as cost-effective pressure on Moscow, while restraint-minded voices question open-ended commitments amid the Middle East war and domestic economic strain, pressing for a negotiated settlement.

Watch for

Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries add a second geopolitical bid to oil markets already jittery over Hormuz. Whether the US ships more interceptors — and whether either capital moves on territory — will shape both the battlefield and energy prices.

Sources: NPR Al Jazeera Washington Post CFR

Data centers become a 2026 campaign flashpoint as Vermont votes today

Facts

  • Vermont holds primary elections today, Aug. 11; Alaska follows Aug. 18, per NPR's election tracker.
  • The energy and water demands of AI data centers have jumped into governor's races: Wisconsin Democrat Francesca Hong and Ohio Republican Vivek Ramaswamy have both called for moratoriums.
  • Early August primaries were mixed — progressives won in Michigan while insurgent Democrats lost in Missouri and Washington.

Left view

NPR and left-leaning outlets frame data-center pushback around ratepayer costs, strained grids and water use, with progressives arguing communities shouldn't subsidize Big Tech's power bills.

Right view

On the right, the concern is often framed around local control, land use and electricity prices for households — notable because a Trump-aligned figure like Ramaswamy landing in the same place as a progressive signals a rare cross-ideological backlash.

Watch for

Expect data-center siting, permitting and utility-rate fights to spread to more statehouses. The bipartisan skepticism could slow the buildout the AI boom depends on — a wildcard for tech capex and power demand forecasts.

Sources: NPR NPR Politics

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: Slipped ~0.1% Monday (Aug 10). Dow: Off ~0.1%. Nasdaq: Down ~0.3% as Nvidia pulled back. Futures edged higher Tuesday on the China tariff extension and easing rate-hike fears.
  • Oil: Jumped roughly 5% Monday as hopes for a Hormuz shipping deal faded; Strait risk keeps crude elevated.
  • Gas: AAA national average about $4.01/gal (Aug 9), down slightly from early-August highs near $4.08 but up sharply year over year.
  • Other: Weak July payrolls (-23k) cut September rate-hike odds to ~44%; next week's CPI is the swing factor. Todd Blanche was confirmed to lead the DOJ 50–49 over the weekend.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: FedEx Cup Playoffs open Thursday with the FedEx St. Jude Championship (Aug 13–16, TPC Southwind), then the BMW Championship and the Tour Championship at East Lake through Aug 30.
  • Tennis: Cincinnati Open (Masters/WTA 1000) is underway Aug 13–23; the draw ceremony was today. Djokovic, Zverev, Medvedev, Fritz and Shelton headline the men's field — a key US Open tune-up.
  • Squash: Mostafa Asal and Hania El Hammamy top the latest PSA world rankings; a PSA World Tour event runs in Valencia this week (Aug 11–15).
  • WWE: Fallout from SummerSlam (Minneapolis, Aug 1–2) continues: CM Punk took the Undisputed title with a shock Randy Orton return, Kevin Owens returned from injury to earn a title shot, and Roman Reigns retained.
  • Hockey: Offseason churn after Carolina's Cup win — Ovechkin re-signed with Washington, Anaheim matched a $90M offer sheet for Leo Carlsson, and Patrick Kane remains unsigned.
  • Soccer: Premier League returns Aug 21; the transfer window closes Sept 1. Newcastle sold Anthony Gordon to Barcelona; Coventry, Hull and Ipswich are the promoted sides.
  • Football: NFL training camps are in full swing with preseason underway. Position battles dominate as teams build toward 53-man rosters; Chiefs, Cardinals and others featured in early camp buzz.

item.title: Mon Aug 10, 2026 — Iran issues steep demands before reopening the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran issues steep demands before reopening the Strait of Hormuz · Iran war splits the MAGA coalition as Trump-Carlson feud deepens · Ukraine's drone campaign triggers Russia's worst fuel crisis in years · Surprise July jobs loss reshapes the Fed's September call
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Iran issues steep demands before reopening the Strait of Hormuz

Facts

  • Iran's national security chief Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr laid out conditions the US must meet before Tehran fully reopens the Strait of Hormuz: lift the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, withdraw American forces from the region, drop sanctions, permanently end the war, and pay compensation for war damage.
  • Iran says it is close to a deal with Oman on managing the strait, but is holding out for US concessions first.
  • Over the weekend a vessel owned by Abu Dhabi's state oil company ADNOC was struck while transiting the strait; Iran's foreign ministry acknowledged firing on commercial shipping.
  • Trump said the strait would reopen "soon" or he would order a fresh attack, and predicted gas prices would fall once the war ends. Iran confirms messages are passing through intermediaries but declines to call them negotiations.
  • Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine has privately told administration advisers Washington needs an off-ramp, per CNN reporting.

Left view

NPR and The Guardian frame the conflict as a costly, open-ended "regime change" war with dwindling public support; progressive lawmakers like Rep. Greg Casar call it an illegal war sending "other people's kids" into a senseless fight. Coverage emphasizes the humanitarian and economic toll and the risk of the war widening to Saudi Arabia and Iraq.

Right view

Fox News hosts such as Sean Hannity and Mark Levin remain supportive of pressure on Tehran, while others (Laura Ingraham, Brit Hume) warn the war is becoming an electoral liability. National Review's Jim Geraghty argues the administration "over-promises and under-delivers," and Commentary's John Podhoretz says Trump "chickened out." Fox opinion writers have called any secret deal a "surrender."

Watch for

Analysts warn a prolonged Hormuz closure keeps oil elevated and pressures US pump prices into the fall. A verified Oman-brokered deal could ease crude quickly; renewed strikes or a widening Gulf front (Houthi/Iraqi militia attacks on Saudi and UAE assets) would spike energy prices and rattle shipping insurance markets.

Sources: CNN Fortune CNBC Fox News Al Jazeera

Iran war splits the MAGA coalition as Trump-Carlson feud deepens

Facts

  • The war has fractured Trump's base. Tucker Carlson, a leading 2024 backer, called the US-Israel strikes "evil and disgusting," left the Republican Party in June, and says the war is the biggest presidential mistake of his lifetime.
  • Marjorie Taylor Greene, once a close ally, has become a vocal critic; Megyn Kelly, Steve Bannon and podcaster Joe Rogan have also questioned the war.
  • Trump has publicly blasted MAGA media figures for criticizing the conflict.
  • VP JD Vance has been deployed to defend the administration's Iran policy, saying the US is in the "middle of the game" on talks.

Left view

MSNBC (ms.now) and Salon highlight the intra-MAGA revolt as evidence the war is politically toxic, casting Carlson's third-party flirtation as a threat to GOP unity heading into the midterms. NPR frames it as antiwar conservatives turning their fire on Trump himself.

Right view

Pro-Trump outlets and hosts (Hannity, Levin) defend the mission and cast critics as naive about Iran; Bannon accuses Fox of "pure propaganda." The Free Press and Reason-adjacent commentators emphasize the "America First" case against foreign entanglement, arguing the war betrays the non-interventionist promise Trump ran on.

Watch for

Strategists see the split as a real midterm risk: a Carlson-aligned third-party push could siphon populist voters. Watch whether Fox's editorial line hardens toward an exit, and whether GOP candidates in competitive districts distance themselves from the war.

Sources: Wikipedia TIME The Hill MSNBC Fox News

Ukraine's drone campaign triggers Russia's worst fuel crisis in years

Facts

  • Ukraine has hit Russian oil refineries with long-range drones almost daily for months, targeting facilities including Ryazan (a main fuel artery to Moscow) and Volgograd.
  • Independent analysts describe the most severe Russian fuel crisis in years; the pace and coordination of strikes leaves Russia unable to repair refineries before the next wave.
  • Gasoline shortages that began in Crimea and the far east have spread to the Volga region and central and southern Russia, per Reuters-cited retailers and traders.
  • The strikes are unsettling the Russian public far from the front lines.

Left view

The Guardian and CNN emphasize the strategic logic: hitting Russia's war economy and energy revenue to pressure Moscow toward the table, while noting the toll on ordinary Russians and the risk of escalation.

Right view

Right-leaning and hawkish commentators frame the campaign as proof Ukraine can impose real costs and argue it validates continued Western support for long-range capabilities; some caution about global oil-price spillover and escalation risk if Russian energy exports are further disrupted.

Watch for

Energy analysts warn sustained refinery damage could tighten global diesel and gasoline supply and add upward pressure on prices already elevated by the Hormuz crisis. Watch for Russian retaliation, export curbs, and any impact on winter fuel supplies inside Russia.

Sources: CNN Wikipedia Fortune Kyiv Post Al Jazeera

Surprise July jobs loss reshapes the Fed's September call

Facts

  • The US economy unexpectedly shed 23,000 jobs in July, far below the forecast gain of about 83,000.
  • Average hourly earnings rose just 2 cents; the 12-month wage figure eased to 3.2%, the lowest since May 2021.
  • Markets moved sharply: after the report, CME FedWatch showed roughly a 56% chance the Fed holds rates at 3.5%-3.75% in September, with odds of a hike falling to about 44%. Treasury yields dropped.
  • Stocks rallied on the news; the S&P 500 closed at a record 7,757.64 on Aug. 7 and topped 7,700 for the first time this week.

Left view

NPR and other outlets frame the weak print as a warning sign that tariffs and the war are cooling the labor market, arguing the Fed should hold or ease to protect jobs rather than fight sticky inflation on workers' backs.

Right view

Fox Business and market-focused conservatives stress that inflation remains elevated and "sticky," warning the Fed shouldn't over-read one soft month; some tie the softness to policy uncertainty and argue for pro-growth measures over rate cuts.

Watch for

Next week's inflation data is the swing factor. A hot CPI would revive hike talk despite the weak jobs number; a cool print cements a hold. Economists warn of a stagflation-style bind — soft growth plus sticky prices — with markets currently betting the Fed stays put.

Sources: CNBC Fox Business Yahoo Finance Forbes

Wildfires and smoke blanket the western US and Canada

Facts

  • Evacuation orders are in place across parts of the western US and southwest Canada amid hot, dry conditions.
  • The National Interagency Fire Center reported 183 new US wildfires, eight of them large, since Saturday; the US has seen 29,023 fires burning about 2.35 million acres in 2026.
  • Canada had roughly 900 active fires with over 3.3 million hectares burned this year; British Columbia alone had more than 100 active fires.
  • Canadian wildfire smoke continues to spread across the US Midwest and Northeast, degrading air quality for millions.

Left view

NPR and Yale Climate Connections tie the intensifying fire and smoke seasons to climate change, calling the smoke event historic and pressing for emissions action and stronger public-health protections.

Right view

Right-leaning coverage tends to emphasize forest-management and land-use policy, prescribed burns, and preparedness over climate framing, focusing on protecting communities and firefighting resources.

Watch for

Air-quality alerts across the Midwest and Northeast, strain on firefighting resources, and downstream effects on insurance, tourism and outdoor labor. A hot, dry late summer would extend the season and the smoke.

Sources: NPR CBC Newsweek Yale Climate

Blanche installed atop DOJ as 2026 primary season heats up

Facts

  • The Senate confirmed Todd Blanche, Trump's former personal lawyer, to lead the Justice Department in a 50-49 vote early Saturday, Aug. 8.
  • Primary season is reshaping Congress: nine House members have lost primaries in 2026 and 62 more aren't seeking re-election.
  • Results have been mixed for insurgents — progressives won in Michigan while voters in Missouri and Washington rejected some insurgent Democrats.
  • Upcoming contests include Vermont (Aug. 11) and Alaska (Aug. 18); Trump has endorsed Mike Lindell in Minnesota's governor primary.

Left view

NBC News and NPR frame Blanche's confirmation as further politicization of the Justice Department by installing a Trump loyalist, and read the primaries as a test of the party's progressive vs. establishment direction under wartime pressure.

Right view

Conservative outlets present Blanche as a needed reformer to clean up a DOJ they view as weaponized, and cast GOP primary turnout as a sign of base energy — while noting Trump-endorsed candidates like Lindell test the limits of loyalty politics.

Watch for

Blanche's early personnel and case decisions will signal DOJ direction. The Vermont and Alaska primaries, plus Minnesota's governor race, offer fresh reads on whether the Iran war is moving voters ahead of November.

Sources: NBC News NPR Wikipedia

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: Record close of 7,757.64 on Aug. 7 (+0.62%), up ~3.6% on the week. Dow: 54,036.93 (+0.28%), just off a record. Nasdaq: 26,690.62 (+1.30%), up ~5.2% on the week as chip stocks bounced.
  • Fed: After the weak July jobs report, markets price ~56% odds of a September hold at 3.5%-3.75%; hike odds fell to ~44%. Treasury yields dropped.
  • Oil: Elevated on the Hormuz standoff and the ADNOC tanker strike; a Gulf shipping disruption keeps a risk premium in crude.
  • Gas: AAA national average about $4.06-$4.08/gal, up ~28 cents from a month ago and well above ~$3.14 a year ago. Trump says prices fall when the war ends.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: FedEx Cup Playoffs tee off this week — FedEx St. Jude Championship (Aug. 13-16, Memphis), then BMW Championship and the Tour Championship, with a $25M bonus to the champion.
  • Tennis: Cincinnati Open (Masters 1000 / WTA 1000) runs Aug. 13-23 in Mason, Ohio; Djokovic, Zverev, Fritz, Shelton and Auger-Aliassime headline the men's field. Draw is Tuesday.
  • Squash: PSA off-season, but World Championship qualifying events are on the calendar — Karachi (Aug. 11-15), with Valencia and Budapest later this month.
  • WWE: Fallout from SummerSlam (Aug. 1-2, Minneapolis): Roman Reigns retained the World Title over Seth Rollins, Chelsea Green won the inaugural Women's Interim Title, and Kevin Owens returned on SmackDown as No. 1 contender.
  • Hockey: NHL offseason churns on after Carolina's first Cup since 2006 — Ovechkin re-signed with Washington (1 yr), Marchment to San Jose; Robertson, Fantilli and Patrick Kane still unsigned.
  • Soccer: Premier League 2026/27 kicks off Aug. 21 (Arsenal vs. Coventry), pushed a week later by the summer World Cup; Community Shield (Arsenal vs. Man City) is Aug. 16 in Cardiff.
  • Football: NFL camps are in full swing — Vikings' Murray vs. McCarthy QB battle, Packers' RB room in flux with Josh Jacobs banged up; regular season kicks off Sept. 9 (Patriots at Seahawks).

item.title: Sun Aug 9, 2026 — Senate confirms Todd Blanche as attorney general in a 50–49 squeaker
item.description: Senate confirms Todd Blanche as attorney general in a 50–49 squeaker · Strait of Hormuz standoff drags on as Iran floats stricter transit terms · US economy sheds 23,000 jobs in July, reshaping the Fed debate · Progressive El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate primary, a blow to AIPAC
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Senate confirms Todd Blanche as attorney general in a 50–49 squeaker

Facts

  • The Senate voted 50–49 early Saturday to confirm Todd Blanche, President Trump's former personal criminal-defense lawyer, as the 88th U.S. attorney general.
  • Republicans Susan Collins (Maine) and Lisa Murkowski (Alaska) broke ranks to oppose him; the rest was a party-line vote.
  • Holdout concerns centered on Blanche's handling of the release of Jeffrey Epstein-related documents and his role in a roughly $1.8B "anti-weaponization" fund tied to the president.

Left view

Outlets like The Washington Post and The Hill frame it as installing a Trump loyalist atop DOJ; Sen. Adam Schiff argued (via Al Jazeera coverage) that an AG shouldn't see his job as enriching the president or pursuing his political enemies.

Right view

The White House called the confirmation "great news," and Roll Call notes supporters like Sen. Cassidy ultimately backed him, casting the Epstein and fund objections as overblown and arguing Trump is entitled to his pick for DOJ.

Watch for

Analysts expect early tests over Epstein-file disclosures, DOJ independence, and any moves touching Trump's legal or political adversaries. The two GOP defections signal a thin margin for future contested nominations.

Sources: Washington Post Roll Call The Hill Al Jazeera

Strait of Hormuz standoff drags on as Iran floats stricter transit terms

Facts

  • The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed to routine commercial shipping since late July, after a June US–Iran arrangement broke down. Traffic ran near 10 vessels a day versus a pre-crisis 88–130.
  • Iran and Oman say they agreed on coordinates for shipping routes, but Iran's draft plan reportedly seeks to exclude US and Israeli vessels and charge fees, which Washington calls unacceptable.
  • Brent crude sat around $83/barrel; Trump said the war "can't go much longer" and predicted gas prices would fall once it ends.

Left view

Progressive voices (MSNBC/MS NOW's Rachel Maddow) argue Trump keeps shifting his rationale for the war while easing pressure on Russia even as Moscow aids Iran; the war-skeptical Washington Examiner op-ed page says the US "can't afford" the conflict.

Right view

The administration insists Iran's military is "in ruins" and that the US imports almost no Hormuz oil; hawks want unrestricted transit and reject Iranian tolls, while some MAGA figures (per NPR reporting) openly criticize Trump for risking a "forever war."

Watch for

Energy analysts say a credible Iran–Oman deal could return millions of barrels to market and pull gas prices lower, while a collapse could spike Brent. Rising pump prices are feeding GOP midterm anxiety.

Sources: Al Jazeera CNBC PBS NewsHour Washington Examiner Background

US economy sheds 23,000 jobs in July, reshaping the Fed debate

Facts

  • Nonfarm payrolls fell 23,000 in July versus expectations of about +83,000, per the Bureau of Labor Statistics; May and June were revised down by a combined 103,000.
  • Unemployment ticked down to 4.1%, but largely because people left the labor force. Annual wage growth slipped to 3.2%, the lowest since 2021.
  • Traders cut September rate-hike odds from 57% to 44%; the debate shifted from whether the Fed hikes to whether it pauses or eventually cuts.

Left view

Democrats (Rep. Nancy Pelosi, Common Dreams) call it proof "the Trump economy has failed," pointing to slowing wages and downward revisions as signs tariffs and policy are damaging growth.

Right view

The White House (via Fox News framing) touts manufacturing and factory-construction gains and record-low jobless claims; NEC director Kevin Hassett tied shrinking payrolls partly to the deportation push reducing the labor force.

Watch for

Economists say another soft print could push the Fed toward a cut this fall. Stocks actually rallied on "bad news is good news" logic (see below); watch August CPI and jobless claims for confirmation.

Sources: CNBC Yahoo Finance BLS The Hill Common Dreams

Progressive El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate primary, a blow to AIPAC

Facts

  • Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, a former Michigan public-health official, won the Democratic Senate nomination Aug. 4 by roughly a point over Rep. Haley Stevens in the most expensive Senate primary in US history.
  • He overcame about $65M in outside spending, including more than $30M from AIPAC-aligned groups backing Stevens.
  • He faces Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers in November; the race could help decide Senate control.

Left view

NBC News and CNN cast it as a Midwest beachhead for a resurgent progressive left; Al Jazeera frames it as a rebuke of AIPAC's spending in Democratic primaries.

Right view

Conservatives argue a Medicare-for-All, corporate-money-critical nominee is too far left for a swing state and hands Rogers an opening, casting the result as evidence of a Democratic fracture heading into the midterms.

Watch for

Michigan becomes a marquee general-election battleground. Watch whether national Democrats consolidate behind El-Sayed and how AIPAC recalibrates after a high-profile loss.

Sources: NBC News CNN Al Jazeera Ballotpedia

Stocks hit records as weak jobs data fuels a rate-cut rally

Facts

  • The S&P 500 closed at a record 7,757.64 Friday (+0.62%); the Nasdaq rose 1.3% to 26,690.62 and the Dow added 152 points to 54,036.93 after topping 54,000 for the first time earlier in the week.
  • For the week the S&P gained 3.6% and the Nasdaq 5.2%, powered by a rebound in chip stocks.
  • The rally accelerated after the soft jobs report lowered expectations for Fed tightening.

Left view

Left-leaning commentators warn the record highs mask a weakening labor market and a widening gap between Wall Street and workers, cautioning that a cooling economy — not strength — is driving the melt-up.

Right view

The administration and market bulls (via CNBC/Fox framing) credit strong corporate earnings and pro-growth policy, arguing "doom" predictions were again proven wrong as indexes set records.

Watch for

Strategists note the "bad news is good news" trade depends on the Fed easing; a hot inflation print or a Hormuz oil spike could reverse sentiment fast. Chip-sector momentum remains the swing factor.

Sources: CNBC CNN Business Bloomberg

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: record 7,757.64 (+0.62% Fri, +3.6% wk). Dow: 54,036.93 (+152). Nasdaq: 26,690.62 (+1.3%, +5.2% wk).
  • Oil: Brent ~$83/bbl, still elevated on Hormuz uncertainty and Iran's stricter draft transit plan.
  • Gas: AAA national average ~$4.02/gal (Aug. 8), easing on lower crude but up from ~$3.80 a month ago. California highest (~$5.64), Indiana lowest (~$3.57).
  • Rates: Odds of a September Fed hike fell to ~44% after the July jobs miss; markets now weigh a possible pause or cut.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: FedExCup Playoffs open this week — FedEx St. Jude Championship at TPC Southwind (Aug. 13–16), top 70 in the points race qualify.
  • Tennis: Cincinnati Open main draw runs Aug. 13–23; Sinner headlines as World No. 1 while defending champ Alcaraz has withdrawn.
  • Squash: PSA offseason lull — World Championship qualifiers and events in Valencia, Budapest and Karachi dot the late-August calendar as the 2026–27 season ramps up.
  • WWE: SummerSlam fallout continues — CM Punk took the Undisputed Title from Cody Rhodes (with a Randy Orton return), Oba Femi beat Brock Lesnar in Hell in a Cell, and Kevin Owens returned to earn a title shot.
  • Hockey: Offseason churn after Carolina's first Cup since 2006 — Ovechkin re-signed in Washington (1yr, $4.25M AAV), Anaheim matched Leo Carlsson's $90M offer sheet, and Patrick Kane remains a free agent.
  • Soccer: Premier League preseason winding up ahead of the Aug. 21 opener; the window closes Sept. 1. Chelsea signed Valentin Barco; Man City's Rodri to miss camp start after minor back surgery.
  • Football: NFL training camps in week two; the cut to 53-man rosters is due Aug. 30. Season kicks off Sept. 9 with Patriots at defending champ Seahawks in a Super Bowl LX rematch.

item.title: Sat Aug 8, 2026 — July jobs report shocks with a surprise payroll drop, upending the Fed rate debate
item.description: July jobs report shocks with a surprise payroll drop, upending the Fed rate debate · Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan's Democratic Senate primary, a marquee win for the left · Senate passes sweeping Russia sanctions bill, handing Trump broad tariff authority · Gaza ceasefire strains as Israeli strikes draw mediator condemnation
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

July jobs report shocks with a surprise payroll drop, upending the Fed rate debate

Facts

  • Employers unexpectedly shed about 23,000 jobs in July against forecasts near an 83,000 gain, and prior months were revised down by roughly 146,000, per BLS data reported Friday.
  • Government payrolls fell more than 50,000 and leisure/hospitality lost about 40,000, while manufacturing and construction kept adding jobs; the unemployment rate ticked to about 4.1%.
  • Markets flipped from pricing a possible September rate hike to favoring a hold; Treasury yields fell and stocks rallied to records.

Left view

Outlets like NPR and the Washington Post frame the miss as evidence the labor market is cooling under the weight of tariffs and federal workforce cuts, warning the pain is concentrated in public-sector and service jobs.

Right view

Fox Business and allied commentators emphasize resilience in manufacturing and construction and argue the report strengthens the case against further rate hikes, casting weakness as a lagging effect rather than a downturn.

Watch for

Forbes and Indeed Hiring Lab analysts say the coming CPI print is now the swing factor for the Fed's September meeting; a soft inflation number could cement a pause or open the door to cuts, keeping equities bid and pressuring the dollar and yields.

Sources: Fox Business AP/Spokesman Forbes Indeed Hiring Lab

Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan's Democratic Senate primary, a marquee win for the left

Facts

  • Progressive Abdul El-Sayed defeated Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary decided August 5, overcoming heavy outside spending and establishment backing for Stevens.
  • El-Sayed, a former Detroit health official backed by Bernie Sanders, becomes the Democratic nominee for a battleground Senate seat this November.
  • Gov. Gretchen Whitmer had made a late endorsement of Stevens; the race exposed sharp intraparty divides.

Left view

NBC News and the Washington Post cast the result as a Midwest beachhead for a resurgent progressive movement, with grassroots energy overpowering a roughly $65 million establishment effort.

Right view

Fox News highlights El-Sayed's associations with streamer Hasan Piker and past comments on Israel, framing him as too far left to hold the seat; moderate Democrats like Third Way's Matt Bennett echoed alarm, calling the nomination a liability.

Watch for

PBS NewsHour analysts say the general election becomes a test of whether progressive nominees can win statewide in a swing state, shaping Democrats' 2026 Senate map and the party's post-2024 identity fight.

Sources: NBC News Washington Post Fox News PBS NewsHour

Senate passes sweeping Russia sanctions bill, handing Trump broad tariff authority

Facts

  • The Senate voted 86–11 on Friday to pass the "Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026," named for the late senator who long championed it.
  • The bill lets the president impose tariffs up to 100% on major buyers of Russian oil and gas — chiefly China and India — and now moves to the Republican-led House.
  • A Rand Paul–Ron Wyden amendment to strip the new tariff authority failed; the vote followed a deadly Russian missile-and-drone barrage on Kyiv that killed at least 17.

Left view

The Washington Post and NPR frame passage as a bipartisan win for Ukraine's supporters aimed at choking off Moscow's energy revenue, while noting Democrats' unease about expanding Trump's tariff powers.

Right view

Coverage of Rand Paul's opposition (Time, Axios) reflects a libertarian-right worry that the tariffs amount to a tax on Americans and hand the president open-ended trade authority; other Republicans framed it as overdue pressure on Putin.

Watch for

Analysts flag that actual use of the 100% tariff lever against China and India could jolt oil markets and global trade; the House may narrow the tariff provisions, and enforcement timing rests with the White House.

Sources: Washington Post NPR Axios Al Jazeera

Gaza ceasefire strains as Israeli strikes draw mediator condemnation

Facts

  • The October 2025 ceasefire remains formally in place, but near-daily Israeli strikes have continued; mediators Egypt, Qatar and Turkey condemned attacks on healthcare facilities as violations of international law.
  • A US "Board of Peace" envoy met Netanyahu on a Gaza disarmament framework and urged a halt to strikes as talks over a second phase continue.
  • Rights monitors put the post-ceasefire death toll in the hundreds, amid a broader war toll they place above 73,000 since October 2023.

Left view

The Guardian and Al Jazeera emphasize civilian casualties and accuse Israel of repeatedly breaching the truce, arguing Washington's "Israel-first" posture is enabling continued strikes.

Right view

The Washington Times and allied outlets center Hamas disarmament as the sticking point, framing Israeli operations as responses to remaining militant threats and pressure to secure the deal's terms.

Watch for

Diplomats say whether the second phase — disarmament and reconstruction — advances hinges on halting strikes; failure risks a full collapse of the truce and renewed regional escalation.

Sources: Washington Times PBS NewsHour Al Jazeera

Trump signs new orders limiting birthright citizenship

Facts

  • President Trump signed executive orders this week expanding restrictions on birthright citizenship and targeting so-called "birth tourism," following recent court challenges.
  • The moves revive a fight over the 14th Amendment's citizenship guarantee that courts have previously blocked.
  • The administration also advanced deregulation of Head Start rules and new tariff actions on polysilicon imports.

Left view

NBC News and NPR frame the orders as a legally dubious attack on a constitutional guarantee, expecting swift lawsuits and injunctions from immigrant-rights groups and Democratic states.

Right view

Conservative outlets and the White House cast the orders as closing loopholes exploited by "birth tourism" and restoring the original meaning of the 14th Amendment, a longtime priority for immigration hawks.

Watch for

Legal analysts expect the question to move quickly through federal courts and potentially back to the Supreme Court; enforcement is likely stayed pending litigation.

Sources: NPR Washington Post White House

Iran and Oman reach deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz

Facts

  • Iran shared details of an agreement with Oman to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key artery for roughly a fifth of the world's oil, following months of tension after this summer's US–Iran conflict.
  • Trump said the US holds "massive amounts" of munitions, pushing back on reports of depleted stockpiles as he seeks a durable breakthrough with Tehran.
  • The deal builds on earlier US-brokered de-escalation efforts and could ease shipping risk in the Gulf.

Left view

Center-left coverage credits diplomacy and mediation for lowering the risk of a wider war, while cautioning that terms remain thin and reversible.

Right view

Right-leaning commentators frame reopening Hormuz as a product of Trump's maximum-pressure posture and military credibility, arguing strength forced Tehran to the table.

Watch for

Energy analysts say a durable reopening would pull risk premium out of oil and could ease gasoline prices into the fall; any breakdown would quickly reprice crude higher.

Sources: CNN NPR

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: Record close of 7,757.64 Friday (+0.62%), up 3.6% on the week. Dow: 54,036.93 (+151.83, +0.28%), up nearly 3% on the week. Nasdaq: 26,690.62 (+1.3%), up 5.2% on the week on a chip-stock bounce.
  • Drivers: The weak July jobs report cut odds of a September Fed hike; Treasury yields fell and equities rallied to records. SpaceX shares jumped about 12% Friday.
  • Oil: Crude pressured stocks earlier in the week; an Iran–Oman deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could keep a lid on prices if it holds.
  • Gas: AAA national average around $4.02/gal, down from about $4.10 a week ago and $3.85 a month ago, but up sharply from ~$3.14 a year ago.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Wyndham Championship (Aug 6–9) is the regular-season finale before the FedExCup Playoffs; players are scrambling to crack the top 70. Ben James opened with a 62 to sit T-2.
  • Tennis: Between hard-court stops — the Cincinnati Open (ATP/WTA 1000) begins Aug 13 in Mason, Ohio, the last big tune-up before the US Open.
  • Squash: PSA offseason lull; a 2025–26 World Championship Qualifying event for Pan America runs Aug 11–15 as the new tour season ramps up.
  • WWE: SummerSlam fallout (Aug 1–2, Minneapolis): CM Punk took the Undisputed WWE Title from Cody Rhodes with a Randy Orton assist, Kevin Owens returned to earn a title shot, and Roman Reigns retained over Seth Rollins.
  • Hockey: NHL offseason churns on after Carolina's Cup win — Alex Ovechkin re-signed with Washington (1 yr, $4.25M), Claude Giroux is returning to Ottawa, and Patrick Kane remains unsigned.
  • Soccer: Premier League opens Aug 21 with Arsenal defending its first title in 22 years; the transfer window shuts Sep 1. Man City's Rodri is easing back from minor back surgery.
